value.rationale: These five canonical highly symmetric cubic bipartite incidence graphs show a sharp qualitative divide: despite connected self-centered token-jumping optimum spaces, Heawood and Möbius–Kantor are entirely frozen under local slides while Pappus, Desargues and Tutte–Coxeter admit global optimal sliding; their exact diameters and eccentricity profiles inform constrained relocation of minimum monitoring sets. None of this is implied by minimum cardinality alone.
